preamble: With all solutions, one of a group of six men must be exchanged with another of the same group before entry in the grid. The grid entries are all real words.

clue.text: Guy perhaps in awe, portraying revolutionary

definitions.note: a guy is one example of a rope, the line that steadies a tent

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the hidden letters are read backwards
the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of awe and the start of portraying

explanation.surface: Someone stands in awe of a man's portrayal of a revolutionary hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble swaps one chess-piece letter for another before entry: here pawn P becomes bishop B, so ROPE enters as ROBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy rope is a cord that holds a tent or mast steady, so a guy is one kind of rope.

clue.text: Brighten up, brief rush to redevelop

indicators.note: redeveloping rebuilds something in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A short dash to redevelop a site and brighten it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop B becomes the knight N, so REFURBISH enters as REFURNISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To refurbish a room is to renovate and smarten it, making it look fresh again.

clue.text: Calorie-free angel cakes are made by him

indicators.note: being free of something means it is taken out

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer, especially of a stage show
C is the standard abbreviation for a (kilo)calorie on food labels

explanation.surface: Low-calorie angel cakes come from his oven.
explanation.walkthrough: Angel cake is a light sponge, but angel here is a theatrical investor. The king K becomes the rook R, giving BARER.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker is the tradesman whose ovens turn out bread, buns and cakes.

clue.text: Tin boxes about study

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the tin symbol goes round the other piece

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
ca. (circa) means about, used with approximate dates

explanation.surface: Tin boxes are lying about someone's study.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is not the container but the element. The knight N becomes the rook R in the grid, giving SCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a document is to look it over closely, which is a way to study it.

clue.text: Detective breaking vehicle instrument is a cheat

indicators.note: the detective breaks into the words, sitting between them

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a harp is a musical instrument
DS, detective sergeant

explanation.surface: A detective says a vehicle and an instrument reveal who is cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: The pawn P becomes the king K, giving CARDSHARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who wins at cards by trickery, a professional cheat.

clue.text: Language from ancient city getting joke, I see

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
taken as written
the letter C is pronounced like the word see

explanation.surface: A tongue from an old city gets a joke, and the listener understands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' is not understanding but three letters. The pawn P becomes the rook R, giving RUNIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Punic was the Semitic tongue of Carthage, the ancient North African city.

clue.text: Young bird beginning to rehearse for second start of chorus to become cheerful

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another, which signals that one letter replaces another

parts.note: a chick is a baby bird

indicators.note: only the opening letter of chorus is meant; second says it is the second such letter in the bird

parts.note: its opening letter is the one that is swapped out

indicators.note: only the opening letter of rehearse is taken

parts.note: its opening letter is the one swapped in

explanation.surface: A young singer starts rehearsing the chorus and cheers up.
explanation.walkthrough: CHIRK is an old word for to cheer up. The king K becomes the pawn P, so CHIRK enters as CHIRP.
explanation.definitionFit: To chirk, or chirk up, is a dialect verb meaning to brighten in mood and grow lively.

clue.text: Minded, always imprisoned and belted

indicators.note: the word for always is locked inside the other word

parts.note: cared, as in 'minded about it'
e'er, poetic for ever

explanation.surface: A prisoner who was always looked after was also given a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: Belted means sped, not beaten. The rook R becomes the knight N, giving CAREENED.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along headlong, just as to belt along is to go at high speed.

clue.text: One without hope to suffer a swelling endlessly

parts.note: to incur a loss is to suffer it
taken as written

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: a bleb is a small blister or bubble on the skin

explanation.surface: A hopeless person suffering a swelling that will not go down.
explanation.walkthrough: The rook R becomes the knight N, so INCURABLE enters as INCUNABLE, an early printed book.
explanation.definitionFit: An incurable is a patient beyond medical help, someone with no hope of recovery.

clue.text: Late tennis champion's drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Fred Perry, the British Wimbledon champion who died in 1995
second meaning: a cider-like drink fermented from pears

explanation.walkthrough: The champion's name and the pear drink are spelt alike. The second rook R becomes the king K, giving PERKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Perry is an alcoholic drink fermented from pear juice, as cider is from apples, and Fred Perry won Wimbledon three times.

clue.text: Quarrel before European succession

indicators.note: the row comes first, ahead of the letter for European

parts.note: a spat is a petty argument

explanation.surface: A row breaks out ahead of a European royal succession.
explanation.walkthrough: The pawn P becomes the king K, giving SKATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a run of similar events coming one after another, a succession of them.

clue.text: Nothing vulgar and new is cool

parts.note: FA is short for 'sweet FA', a crude British phrase meaning nothing at all

explanation.surface: Something with no vulgarity and novelty is fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: Cool is a verb here, not slang for stylish. The knight N becomes the rook R, so FAN enters as FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To fan something is to blow air over it, which lowers its temperature.

clue.text: Book question or brief answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a brief version is shortened, so only the opening of the word answer is kept

parts.note: only its first two letters are used

explanation.surface: A book of quiz questions that takes brief answers.
explanation.walkthrough: QORAN is a variant spelling of the holy book. The queen Q becomes the king K, giving KORAN in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Qoran is the sacred scripture of Islam, so it is the Book in a religious sense.

clue.text: Front runner returning review

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read from the other end

parts.note: a recap is a short review of what happened

explanation.surface: A candidate leading the race is coming back for another review.
explanation.walkthrough: The pawn P becomes the rook R, so PACER enters as RACER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is an athlete who leads the field to set the speed, a runner at the front.

clue.text: Tells off workers surrounding informer

indicators.note: the workers go round the outside of the informer

parts.note: worker bees, so bees can stand for workers
a rat is someone who tells tales to the authorities

explanation.surface: Staff gather round a snitch and give him a dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop B becomes the rook R, giving RERATES in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate someone is to scold them angrily, the same as telling them off.

clue.text: Upset, carefully ignoring offensive remark, obviously

indicators.note: upset things are knocked over and disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaving out the rude phrase removes those letters from the word

parts.note: the word whose letters are used
F U is a crude abbreviation of an insult

explanation.surface: Someone is clearly upset after carefully steering round a rude comment.
explanation.walkthrough: The rook R becomes the knight N, so CLEARLY enters as CLEANLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearly and obviously are both adverbs saying something is plain to see.

clue.text: State of Quebec paramilitaries at the front

indicators.note: the paramilitaries go first, ahead of the letter from the phonetic alphabet

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army
Quebec is the radio alphabet word for the letter Q

explanation.surface: A province of Canada has paramilitaries on its front line.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks as though it goes with Quebec, a Canadian province, but it is the definition. The queen Q becomes the knight N, giving IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a sovereign country in the Middle East, and a country is a state.

clue.text: One making annulment getting back schedule by bloody short meeting with graduate

indicators.note: the whole string of pieces is turned back to front

parts.note: a rota is a timetable of duties

indicators.note: the word for bloody is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: gory means bloody
BA, Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A judge annuls a marriage after a brief, bloody meeting about a timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop B becomes the rook R, so ABROGATOR enters as ARROGATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate a law or treaty is to repeal it, so an abrogator is one who annuls.

clue.text: Crowd almost drained after return to boozer

indicators.note: the shortened word follows the reversed pub
returning reverses the pub word

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub or bar

indicators.note: almost all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: bled dry, emptied of blood

explanation.surface: A mob, nearly exhausted, heads back to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The rook R becomes the bishop B, so RABBLE enters as BABBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble is a disorderly mob, a crowd of noisy people.

clue.text: Ransacked place below top newsman

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses
under means below
ED, editor, the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A senior journalist's home was ransacked, his place stripped.
explanation.walkthrough: Below looks like a positional instruction but is a word in the answer. The pawn P becomes the bishop B, giving BLUNDERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder a place is to rob it thoroughly, so plundered and ransacked both mean looted.

clue.text: Jumper is poor, not starting to rotate

indicators.note: turning the letters round reads them backwards
the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before the cuts

explanation.surface: A sweater is shoddy and won't spin on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper is not a sweater but an animal: roo is short for kangaroo. The rook R becomes the bishop B, giving BOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A roo, short for kangaroo, is an animal famous for leaping.

clue.text: One moving in the fast lane?

definitions.meaning: a driver or vehicle on the move
the outside lane of a motorway, used for passing slower traffic

explanation.walkthrough: The fast lane suggests a high-flying lifestyle; read literally, it is where cars pass one another. The rook R becomes the knight N, giving OVERTAKEN.
explanation.definitionFit: On a motorway the outer lane is for passing, so whoever drives there is getting past slower cars.

clue.text: Those who cringe from some advertisements — too personal

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken, spanning their joins

parts.note: the letters run from the end of advertisements across too and into personal

explanation.surface: People who wince at adverts that get too intimate.
explanation.walkthrough: The pawn P becomes the king K, giving STOOKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop is to bend low, as people do who cower, so stoopers are those who cringe.

clue.text: Hamburg female?

definitions.meaning: not the German city but a breed of domestic chicken
the female of that breed of fowl

explanation.surface: A woman from the German city of Hamburg.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight N becomes the rook R, so HEN enters as HER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hamburg is a breed of poultry, and a female chicken is a hen.

clue.text: Bribe to hide drug in bandage

indicators.note: the bribe phrase conceals the drug letter inside it

parts.note: to tap up is to approach someone illicitly with an inducement, as when a club poaches a player
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A bribe meant to conceal drugs tucked into a dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tap up is British football slang for luring a contracted player with an illicit offer. The pawn P becomes the king K, giving TAKE-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape up a wound or joint is to bind it with sticky strapping, which is to bandage it.

clue.text: Man's accepting about now …

parts.note: a man is referred to as he, and he is accepting (taking on) the next piece, which follows him
re is the crossword staple for about, as in a letter's 're:' line

explanation.surface: A man is taking on something concerning the present moment, the ellipsis carrying the thought on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' just says the man takes on RE after him. The solved word has its R (rook) swapped for B (bishop), per the preamble's chessmen, so the grid shows HEBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Here can mean at this point in time, as in 'here we go', so it stands for the present moment.

clue.text: Tree surgeon's top exercises adopted by one

indicators.note: being taken in by the word for one places these letters inside it

parts.note: an, the indefinite article meaning one

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is used
PE, physical education

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon's best exercises are taken up by a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight N becomes the rook R, giving ASPER, an old Turkish coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar with trembling leaves, one particular kind of tree.

clue.text: … legendary man making a great impression?

definitions.meaning: a creature of folklore, the ape-man said to roam North American forests
read literally, a huge foot leaves a huge print in the ground

explanation.surface: A famous man who wows everyone he meets.
explanation.walkthrough: A great impression sounds like charisma but means a huge footprint. The bishop B becomes the pawn P in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigfoot, or Sasquatch, is the hairy giant of North American legend known from supposed footprints.

clue.text: More mature killer ignoring one of probationary characters

indicators.note: leaving something out drops one of its doubled letters

parts.note: Jack the Ripper, the notorious Victorian killer
P is the opening character of probationary, as on the P plates of a learner driver who has just passed

explanation.surface: An older killer ignores the terms of his probation.
explanation.walkthrough: The rook R becomes the pawn P, giving PIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Riper is the comparative of ripe, describing fruit or people further along in development.

clue.text: A number working to cut piece of wood

parts.note: ten is a number
on, as in a machine that is switched on and running

explanation.surface: A number of carpenters at work cutting timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight N becomes the rook R, giving TENOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the shaped tongue cut on the end of a timber to fit a mortise joint.

clue.text: Inspector's addressed controversy

parts.note: DI, detective inspector, with the 's attached
a letter that is addressed is sent on its way

explanation.surface: A police inspector has spoken publicly about a row.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight N becomes the rook R, so DISSENT enters as DISSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement with an accepted view, the stuff of controversy.

clue.text: Turn out in English green

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A crowd turns out on an English village green.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn out suggests gathering, but it means to turn inside out. The rook R becomes the knight N, giving EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To evert an organ or eyelid is to turn it outwards, inside out.

clue.text: Wash faces to beautify appearances — the head an eyes

indicators.note: a face is a front, so each following word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words
still under faces: the opening letter of eyes ends the word

explanation.surface: Washing your face to look your best, head and eyes included.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints 'an' where 'and' was probably meant; it plays no part. The bishop B becomes the pawn P in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to wash, whether yourself in a tub or a wound with water.

clue.text: Prize contract

definitions.meaning: first meaning: prize money, as in a boxing purse
second meaning: to pucker or draw together, as with the lips

explanation.walkthrough: Contract looks like a legal agreement but is the verb. The pawn P becomes the knight N, giving NURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse is a sum offered as a reward in sport, and to purse the lips is to pucker them.

clue.text: Even born after setback

indicators.note: set back means put in reverse, so the word reads from its end

parts.note: née, used before a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: Things are level again once someone born has had a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: E'en is the poetic contraction of even. The knight N becomes the king K, so EEN enters as EEK.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse e'en is the shortened form of even, as in 'e'en so'.

clue.text: Cork's holes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Cork is a port, so 'Cork's' reads as 'port's'
second meaning: openings, such as portholes in a ship's side

explanation.walkthrough: Cork looks like a stopper for holes, but it is the Irish harbour city. The pawn P becomes the rook R, giving RORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cork is a harbour city in Ireland, and ports are also openings such as the portholes in a hull.

clue.text: Threaten removing area in home

indicators.note: taking out the letter for area leaves the rest of the dwelling word

parts.note: an abode is a place to live

explanation.surface: Bullying a householder by taking away part of their home.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop B becomes the rook R, so BODE enters as RODE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bode ill is to foretell harm, and something that bodes trouble looms as a menace.

clue.text: Way university's beginning to ban strike

parts.note: U stands for university, as in U3A or a U-card

indicators.note: only the opening letter of ban is taken

parts.note: its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A university starts banning a walkout on its campus road.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike sounds like industrial action but means knocking against something. The bishop B becomes the knight N, giving STUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stub a toe is to strike it against something hard by accident.
